mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) signals robust demand growth, compressing discount rates on equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite upward trend in GDPC1 over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly FEDFUNDS rate crossing above 1% triggers investor expectation of prolonged high rates, leading to short-term selling pressure and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS crossing above 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and decrease in UNRATE signals monetary easing and labor market expansion, both driving positive equity valuations and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite FEDFUNDS increasing and UNRATE decreasing.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, simultaneous high demand (HOUST > 105) and supply (INDPRO > 105) signals overvaluation, but investors anticipate future growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite both HOUST and INDPRO exceeding 105 in the late-cycle regime.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE below 4% signals improving labor market conditions, boosting growth expectations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE falling below 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) and monthly CPIAUCSL signals robust demand growth and inflationary pressures, leading to market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite both GDPC1 and CPIAUCSL increasing.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained FEDFUNDS rates above 2% for 20 trading days signals persistent monetary tightening, raising long-term interest rates and compressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains above 2% for 20 trading days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS remaining above 2% for 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery regime, simultaneous growth in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indicates resurgent economic activity, fostering investor optimism and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite GDPC1 and INDPRO increasing in the post-shock recovery regime.
